verdict.root_cause: At 11:20:03Z platform-automation attached a traffic-shaping (netem-style) sidecar to the cart-service network namespace, imposing a fixed 300ms zero-jitter delay on eth0 in both directions. Every network hop that crosses cartservice's interface therefore pays a constant ~300ms toll: the cartservice→Redis round trip inflates its HGET/HMSET spans to ~301-308ms, and the checkoutservice→cartservice RPC pays the delay on request and response outside the server span, leaving ~900ms per call unaccounted on the client/transport side. Two cart calls per PlaceOrder (GetCart and EmptyCart) at ~1215ms each account for essentially all of the ~2.45-2.49s end-to-end checkout latency. Nothing is erroring — frontend's error ratio is flat zero across the window and productcatalogservice's likewise — and cartservice itself keeps serving normal traffic; the incident is purely a latency regression propagating up from a deliberately slowed network path, surfacing as warnings on cartservice, checkoutservice, frontend and loadgenerator.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent lines converge. The change record (tr_2e272a12abcc) puts a fixed 300ms, zero-jitter delay on cartservice's network interface 3.5 minutes before onset, and explicitly rules out any code deploy, image change, config/flag flip, dependency bump or datastore change in the same window. The traces (tr_4df1c2be82f7) show exactly the signature that change would produce: a constant ~300ms that is identical across read (HGET) and write (HMSET) operations and across traces, sitting at the cartservice-to-Redis hop rather than in application logic, plus a second ~900ms per call that occurs outside the cartservice server span on the checkout→cart transport — i.e. the delay is being paid on the wire, not inside any process. Load-dependent explanations are excluded by the tightness of the distribution, and every other downstream (currency, payment, shipping/quote, product catalog, email, accounting, fraud detection) is sub-27ms, so no other dependency contributes. The failure mode is waiting, not failing: frontend's error ratio is defined and identically zero for all 61 points on both sides of 11:20:03 (tr_e9172af1c9fa), which also rules out timeouts, circuit breaking and connection resets, and productcatalogservice emits zero errors throughout (tr_9629087b16f7), excluding an error cascade seeded upstream. cartservice logs show the process alive and handling multi-request-per-second cart traffic well past onset with no error/warning lines and no datastore complaint (tr_98b777478032), consistent with a healthy process that is merely slow. Per the taxonomy, a setting that inserts delay into a call path is dependency_latency — the wait is the failure — not bad_config, even though a change record sits upstream; the fix is removing the injected shaping, i.e. reverting that change, not rolling back an artifact or restarting a process. Past cart incidents in the corpus are a caution here rather than a match: in both, cartservice's flat-zero error rate was misread as health. Here the same flat-zero reading is corroborated by traces showing cartservice actively serving Redis-backed requests, so the 'cart is fine' inference is not being made on error rate alone.
open_questions: The ~900ms per cart call outside the cartservice server span is attributed to the injected delay on the transport, but no measurement decomposes it — whether it is two 300ms directional applications plus connection setup, or whether a second shaping rule or client-side retry contributes, is unsettled.

cartservice returned no series at all from calls_total under the queried label set (tr_1cbc3a63e9f2); this was never re-queried with the service_name/status_code schema that worked for frontend, so cartservice's own request rate, latency percentiles and error ratio remain entirely unmeasured.

cartservice log output stops at 11:26:17 while the window runs to 11:28:30 (tr_98b777478032, low confidence). Whether this is pod termination, a logging-pipeline stall, or a query artifact is unresolved and could indicate a second, later event.

checkoutservice and loadgenerator alerted at 11:23:45 but neither was measured for error rate; frontend's zero error ratio suggests latency-only, but if those alerts were error-based rather than latency-based, something is unaccounted for.

Why platform-automation created the shaping container — scheduled chaos experiment, misfired automation, or a rule intended for a different target — is not established, and that determines whether reverting is sufficient or the automation will re-apply it.
Request lines with empty user identifiers around 11:26 are unexplained and were not tied to the latency; they may be unrelated.
Four unmeasured edges were crossed by triage and no specialist covered them; whether any service outside the sampled trace path is independently affected is unknown.
